title: Say goodbye: Major chicken chain operator files bankruptcy, closing dozens of locations

 Say goodbye: Major chicken chain operator files bankruptcy, closing dozens of locations
 Published: Nov. 17, 2026, 3:19 p.m. 
 A KFC and Taco Bell franchisee filed for bankruptcy earlier this week along with three affiliates. Court filings show 72 restaurants on the line. Yadi Rodriguez 
 Set as Google Preferred Source 
 By Dallas Gagnon | MassLive.com 
 A franchisee of a popular fried chicken chain and three affiliated companies have filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy , and a list filed with the court shows 72 of its restaurant locations have closed or are closing.
 Tasty Chick’n LLC, an independent KFC and KFC/Taco Bell franchisee based in Plano, Texas, filed Nov. 16 in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Southern District of Texas.
 Three affiliates filed the same day — Tasty Chick’n Midwest LLC, Tasty Chick’n Southeast LLC and VRE Tasty 7 Pack LLC.
 Each petition lists “KFC” and “Kentucky Fried Chicken” as trade names, with Thomas M. Scott, president and CEO, signing each document.
 KFC itself is not in bankruptcy.
 Read more: Fried chicken chain that closed 300 spots has ‘comeback plan’ 
 The three Tasty Chick’n companies each listed between $50 million and $100 million in assets and between $100 million and $500 million in liabilities.
 VRE Tasty 7 Pack LLC listed between $500,001 and $1 million in both.
 The company says it currently owns or operates 84 restaurants in 10 states. It didn’t say how many of the 72 locations are among those.
 Which locations have closed or are closing
 The company asked the court to let it drop leases at 72 restaurants it says have either “already shut down” or are “winding down business and will no longer be operating.”
 Read more: Major pizza chain operator files bankruptcy, leaving 15 stores in limbo 
 At some locations, it left the keys in lockboxes for landlords.
 The filings don’t say which restaurants are already closed. A judge must approve the lease rejections; a hearing was set for Nov. 17.

 Why did they file?
 Sales fell 11.4% in 2024, 1.4% in 2025 and 2.8% so far in 2026 while costs rose, according to a sworn declaration from Scott.
 The company largely stopped paying royalties in November 2025. In September, KFC and Taco Bell moved to end the franchise agreements over $15.7 million in unpaid fees, which would strip the company’s right to use the brands.
 It also owes about $67.2 million to its main lenders.
 The filing comes a week after a Papa Johns franchisee and four affiliates filed for bankruptcy, putting 15 restaurants in Pennsylvania and Ohio in question.
